reason: The text contains multiple explicitly named characters who are regular people. Joseph (יוֹסֵף) is the primary named character and is clearly portrayed as a human with agency, emotions, and relationships - he serves as a slave, experiences attraction and moral conflict, and later becomes an administrator. Potiphar (פּוֹטִיפַר) is another named character, described as an Egyptian official and captain of the guard. Both are human characters with personal narratives, not divine or supernatural beings. While they occupy positions of authority or servitude, they are nonetheless regular people within the narrative framework.
